title: The Bias Variance Decomposition of Prediction Error
subject: Machine Learning
statement: For squared error regression the expected test error at a point is noise variance plus squared bias plus model variance.
short: Prediction error splits into noise, bias and variance.
detail: Flexible models lower bias but raise variance.
proof: Expand around the true mean and use independence of noise.
consequence: Explains why minimizing training error can hurt.

title: Empirical Risk Minimization
subject: Machine Learning
statement: ERM selects the hypothesis minimizing average loss on the training sample.
short: Learn by minimizing average training loss.
detail: It replaces unknown expected risk by its empirical estimate.
proof: Define empirical risk as a sample mean and minimize.

title: Optimistic Bias of Training Error
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Training error underestimates test error because the same data selected the hypothesis.
short: A model judged on its own training data looks too good.
proof: The minimizing hypothesis has unusually small empirical loss.

title: K Fold Cross Validation
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Split data into k folds, train on the rest and validate on each fold in turn, then average.
short: Rotate the validation fold and average errors.
detail: Common choices are five and ten folds.
proof: Retrain once per fold and average validation losses.
consequence: Estimates error when data are scarce.

title: Leave One Out Cross Validation
subject: Machine Learning
statement: LOO uses each single observation as a validation set in turn.
short: Validate on one point at a time.
detail: Nearly unbiased but high variance and costly.
proof: Retrain n times omitting one sample.

title: Ridge Regression Closed Form
subject: Machine Learning
statement: L2 penalized least squares has the closed form w equals X transpose X plus lambda I inverse times X transpose y.
detail: The penalty stabilizes ill conditioned fits.
proof: Set the penalized gradient to zero.

title: Lasso Induces Sparsity
subject: Machine Learning
statement: An L1 penalty tends to set some coefficients exactly to zero.
detail: The L1 ball has corners aligned with axes.
proof: Zero is optimal when correlation with the residual is below lambda.

title: Soft Thresholding for Orthogonal Lasso
subject: Machine Learning
statement: With an orthonormal design the lasso solution soft thresholds ordinary least squares coefficients.
proof: Minimize each quadratic plus absolute value term explicitly.

title: Logistic Regression Model
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Logistic regression models a class probability with a linear score passed through a sigmoid.
short: A linear model with sigmoid output.
detail: It is a discriminative probabilistic classifier.
proof: Apply the logistic link to a linear predictor.

title: Logistic Loss Is Convex
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Negative log likelihood of logistic regression is convex in the weights.
detail: The Hessian is a positive semidefinite weighted Gram matrix.
proof: Compute the Hessian as X transpose D X.
consequence: Gradient methods reach a global optimum.

title: Cross Entropy Is Bernoulli Negative Log Likelihood
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Minimizing binary cross entropy equals maximizing Bernoulli likelihood.
short: Cross entropy is the natural loss for probabilities.

title: Naive Bayes Independence Assumption
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Naive Bayes assumes features are conditionally independent given the class.
short: Pretend features are independent within a class.
detail: The assumption is usually false but often harmless.
proof: Apply the chain rule and drop feature dependences.
consequence: Makes high dimensional density estimation easy.

title: Naive Bayes Zero Probability Failure
subject: Machine Learning
statement: An unseen feature value in a class makes the naive Bayes posterior exactly zero.
short: One zero factor erases a class.
consequence: Smoothing is essential for categorical data.

title: K Nearest Neighbors Classifier
subject: Machine Learning
statement: kNN classifies by majority vote among the k closest training points.
detail: Distance metric and k are key choices.
proof: Compute distances, pick k smallest, take the mode.

title: Cover Hart Consistency of Nearest Neighbors
subject: Machine Learning
statement: If k grows and k over n tends to zero, kNN is asymptotically Bayes optimal under mild conditions.
short: Neighbours eventually win with enough data.
detail: Bias shrinks as the region shrinks and variance shrinks as it grows.
proof: Balance the two effects using regularity of the distribution.

title: Decision Tree Split by Impurity Reduction
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Trees greedily choose splits that most reduce impurity such as Gini or entropy.
short: Split on the feature separating classes best.
detail: Greedy splitting is not globally optimal.
proof: Evaluate candidate splits and keep the largest gain.

title: Gini Impurity
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Gini impurity is the probability of mislabeling a random element under the node distribution.
proof: Sum the chance of each label times a different label.

title: Entropy and Information Gain
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Shannon entropy measures label uncertainty and information gain is its reduction after a split.
short: Gain is entropy before minus after.
detail: Used by ID3 to choose attributes.
proof: Compute weighted child entropies and subtract.

title: Pruning Combats Tree Overfitting
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Deep trees fit noise so limiting depth or pruning improves test performance.
short: Stop early or cut back branches.
proof: A branch fitted to few examples captures noise.

title: Bootstrap Aggregating
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Bagging trains models on bootstrap resamples and averages predictions.
short: Average models trained on resampled data.
detail: Helps unstable learners such as trees.
proof: Draw B bootstrap samples and aggregate.
consequence: Improves accuracy of high variance learners.

title: Why Bagging Reduces Variance
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Averaging independent models reduces variance roughly by the number of models.
short: Many independent predictions average out noise.
proof: Use linearity of variance for independent terms.

title: Random Forest
subject: Machine Learning
statement: A random forest averages trees grown on bootstrap samples with random feature subsets at each split.
proof: Grow each tree with rows and feature subsampling.

title: AdaBoost
subject: Machine Learning
statement: AdaBoost reweights misclassified examples and combines weak learners by weighted vote.
short: Focus later learners on hard examples.
detail: Each learner sees a reweighted dataset.
proof: Train greedily to reduce exponential loss.
consequence: Turns weak learners into a strong one.

title: AdaBoost Training Error Bound
subject: Machine Learning
statement: If every weak learner has weighted error bounded below one half, AdaBoost training error decays exponentially.
detail: Bound exponential loss then relate it to zero one error.
proof: Track multiplicative loss decrease per round.

title: Gradient Boosting
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Gradient boosting fits each new model to the negative gradient of the loss at current predictions.
short: Boosting as gradient descent in function space.
proof: Approximate the negative gradient with a base learner.

title: Maximum Margin Linear Classifier
subject: Machine Learning
statement: An SVM chooses the separating hyperplane maximizing minimum distance to training points.
detail: Maximizing margin equals minimizing norm under constraints.
proof: Distance to a hyperplane is w transpose x plus b over norm.

title: Margin Width Equals Two Over Norm
subject: Machine Learning
statement: With margin constraints y_i times score at least one the geometric margin is two over the weight norm.
proof: Distance between score plus and minus one is two over norm.

title: Hinge Loss
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Hinge loss penalizes predictions within a margin of the correct label and is zero beyond it.
consequence: Convex surrogate for zero one loss.

title: Support Vectors Determine the Boundary
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Only points on or inside the margin affect the learned SVM hyperplane.
short: Most data can be discarded after training.
detail: Complementary slackness forces other dual weights to zero.

title: The Kernel Trick
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Kernels compute inner products in a feature space without forming feature vectors.
detail: Inner product algorithms can be kernelized.
proof: Replace inner products by a valid kernel.
consequence: Enables nonlinear models with linear machinery.

title: Representer Theorem
subject: Machine Learning
statement: The minimizer of regularized empirical risk in an RKHS is a finite combination of kernel sections at the data.
short: Infinite search collapses to n coefficients.
proof: Project onto the span of data kernels.

title: RBF Kernel Has Infinite Features
subject: Machine Learning
statement: The Gaussian kernel corresponds to an infinite dimensional feature map.
short: A finite kernel encodes infinitely many features.
proof: Use the Taylor series of the exponential.

title: Positive Semidefinite Kernels Are Valid
subject: Machine Learning
statement: A symmetric kernel defines inner products in some feature space exactly when its Gram matrix is positive semidefinite.
short: PSD is the validity condition for kernels.
detail: Build features from a spectral decomposition.
proof: Apply Mercer theorem or finite Gram characterization.

title: Kernel Ridge Regression Closed Form
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Kernel ridge regression predicts with coefficients equal to the inverse of K plus n lambda I times y.
short: Ridge regression has a feature space formula.
detail: Apply the representer theorem and solve.
proof: Substitute the kernel expansion into the objective.

title: Gaussian Process Mean Matches Kernel Ridge
subject: Machine Learning
statement: The Gaussian process posterior mean has the same form as kernel ridge regression.
short: GP regression is a kernel smoother.
detail: Compare posterior mean with representer form.
proof: Identify noise variance with ridge parameter.

title: Accuracy Paradox under Imbalance
subject: Machine Learning
statement: With 99 percent negatives an always negative classifier has 99 percent accuracy and zero positive recall.
detail: Accuracy is dominated by the majority class.
proof: Compute the confusion matrix of the trivial rule.
consequence: Use precision recall or AUC instead.

title: Precision Recall and F1
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Precision is TP over TP plus FP, recall is TP over TP plus FN, and F1 is their harmonic mean.

title: ROC Curve and AUC
subject: Machine Learning
statement: ROC plots true positive rate against false positive rate across thresholds and AUC is its area.
detail: It equals the chance a positive outranks a negative.

title: Label Smoothing
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Replacing hard targets by soft labels can improve calibration and generalization empirically.
detail: It is a heuristic rather than a theorem.

title: One Hot Encoding
subject: Machine Learning
statement: One hot encoding maps a category to a vector with one 1 and zeros elsewhere.
proof: Map each category to a basis vector.

title: Holdout Validation
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Reserving a random test set untouched by training gives an unbiased error estimate.
short: Reserve data never used for fitting.
detail: Reusing the test set for tuning invalidates it.
proof: Training and test samples are independent.

title: Hyperparameter Search
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Hyperparameters such as tree depth are chosen by validation performance rather than training fit.
proof: Evaluate candidate settings on a split.

title: Data Leakage Inflates Results
subject: Machine Learning
statement: If test information enters preprocessing, validation scores become optimistically biased.
proof: Trace information into the fitted model.

title: Feature Scaling for Gradient Methods
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Features on very different scales distort distances and slow gradient descent.
detail: It is a heuristic, not a universal theorem.

title: Selection Bias in Cross Validation
subject: Machine Learning
statement: The best score among many tuned models is an optimistic estimate of true performance.
detail: Selection on noisy scores favours luck.
proof: Maxima of noisy estimates are upward biased.

title: Bayesian Linear Regression Predictive Mean
subject: Machine Learning
statement: With a Gaussian prior on weights the posterior predictive mean equals ridge regression predictions.
detail: The prior acts as a quadratic penalty.

title: The Bootstrap Estimates Variability
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Resampling with replacement approximates the sampling distribution of a statistic.
proof: Draw samples with replacement and recompute.

title: Bagging Needs Unstable Learners
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Bagging helps high variance learners and can do nothing for stable ones.

title: Early Stopping as Regularization
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Stopping iterative training before convergence can improve generalization.
detail: It is an implicit regularization heuristic.

title: Softmax Regression
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Softmax regression models each class probability with exponentials of linear scores normalized by their sum.

title: Log Sum Exp Is a Smooth Maximum
subject: Machine Learning
statement: Log sum exp is a smooth convex approximation to the maximum.
detail: Bounds follow by factoring the largest term.

title: Empirical Risk Minimization Can Overfit
subject: Machine Learning
statement: A class that shatters a sample can fit arbitrary labels with zero training error and no generalization guarantee.
short: Perfect training fit need not predict well.
detail: Noise or random labels can be memorized.
proof: Construct a classifier matching any labelling.

title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Empirically, sparse subnetworks within a trained network can be retrained from their initial weights to match dense performance.
detail: It is an empirical observation with ongoing theoretical study.
proof: Prune small magnitude weights and retrain.

title: Grokking in Algorithmic Tasks
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: On small algorithmic datasets test accuracy can jump long after training accuracy is perfect.
detail: It is an empirical phenomenon, not a theorem.
proof: Track train and test curves over long training.

title: Neural Networks Memorize Random Labels
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Large networks can fit training data even when labels are randomized.
detail: It is an empirical observation with theoretical analyses.
proof: Train on shuffled labels and observe fit.
consequence: Shows optimization is not the only limit.

title: The Effectiveness of Large Data
subject: Machine Learning
statement: In many tasks simple models trained on very large data outperform more elaborate models trained on little data.
detail: It is an empirical observation, not a theorem.
proof: Compare scaling curves across model families.

title: Simplicity Bias in Training
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Neural networks empirically tend to learn simpler functions early in training.
detail: It is an empirical observation with partial theory.
proof: Observe learned functions over training time.

title: EM as Coordinate Ascent on the ELBO
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: EM is coordinate ascent on the evidence lower bound with the distribution set to the exact posterior in the E step.
short: The E step closes the KL gap.
detail: Maximize ELBO over q then theta.
proof: Take q equal p of z given x and theta.

title: Linear Autoencoders Learn PCA
subject: Neural Networks
statement: A linear autoencoder with tied weights spans the same subspace as principal component analysis.
detail: The orthogonal Procrustes problem gives this result.
consequence: Links classical statistics and neural nets.

title: Shannon Entropy Measures Code Length
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Shannon entropy gives the expected code length of an optimal prefix code up to one bit.
proof: Round log probabilities to integer lengths.

title: The Perceptron
subject: Neural Networks
statement: A perceptron computes a weighted sum, adds a bias and outputs a sign.
detail: Its update adds a misclassified example to the weight vector.

title: Perceptron Convergence Theorem
subject: Neural Networks
statement: For linearly separable data with margin gamma and bounded norm the perceptron makes at most R squared over gamma squared mistakes.
short: Separable data guarantee finitely many mistakes.
detail: Track alignment with a separator and weight norm growth.
proof: Compare the dot product and squared norm bounds.

title: Perceptron Fails on XOR
subject: Neural Networks
statement: XOR is not linearly separable so a single perceptron cannot represent it.
detail: The four points cannot be split by one line.
proof: Solve the four inequalities and derive a contradiction.

title: Backpropagation
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Backpropagation computes gradients by applying the chain rule backwards through the computational graph.
short: Propagate error signals from output to input.
proof: Apply multivariate chain rule in reverse order.

title: Gradient of an Affine Layer
subject: Neural Networks
statement: For an affine layer followed by activation the weight gradient is the outer product of upstream error and layer input.
detail: Differentiate W a plus b with respect to W.
proof: Follow the chain rule through the affine map.

title: Universal Approximation Theorem
subject: Neural Networks
statement: A feedforward net with one hidden layer and a nonconstant bounded sigmoid like activation approximates any continuous function on a compact set arbitrarily well.
short: One hidden layer suffices for approximation.
detail: It is a representation result, not a learning guarantee.
proof: Use a Stone Weierstrass style argument.

title: Approximation Is Not Learnability
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Existence of an approximating network says nothing about finding it from finite data by gradient descent.
short: Expressivity is not optimization or generalization.
detail: The theorem is nonconstructive about samples.

title: ReLU Activation
subject: Neural Networks
statement: ReLU outputs the positive part of its input.
detail: It is cheap and avoids positive saturation.

title: Dying ReLU Problem
subject: Neural Networks
statement: ReLU units with negative pre activation can receive zero gradient and stop updating.
short: Some neurons can get stuck off.
proof: A zero derivative blocks the gradient path.

title: Sigmoid Saturation Slows Learning
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Sigmoid derivatives vanish for large magnitude inputs causing slow gradient flow.

title: Hyperbolic Tangent Activation
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Tanh maps inputs to the interval minus one to one and is zero centered.
detail: Its derivative is one minus tanh squared.

title: Leaky ReLU
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Leaky ReLU gives a small nonzero slope for negative inputs.
short: Keeps a gradient for negative inputs.
proof: Define a two slope piecewise linear function.

title: Softmax Function
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Softmax converts logits into probabilities by exponentiating and normalizing.
detail: Subtract the maximum logit for stability.

title: Softmax Cross Entropy Gradient
subject: Neural Networks
statement: The gradient of softmax cross entropy with respect to logits is predicted probability minus target.

title: Convolutional Layer
subject: Neural Networks
statement: A convolutional layer applies the same small kernel at every spatial location.
short: Shared local filters slide over input.
proof: Slide kernel and compute dot products.

title: Weight Sharing Reduces Parameters
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Convolution ties weights across positions, reducing parameters versus a fully connected layer.

title: Convolution Is Translation Equivariant
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Shifting the input shifts a convolutional feature map by the same amount up to boundaries.
short: Shift the image, shift the features.

title: Pooling Operation
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Pooling replaces a local region by a summary such as maximum or average.
proof: Partition into regions and reduce each.

title: Recurrent Neural Network
subject: Neural Networks
statement: An RNN applies the same transition at each time step while carrying a hidden state.
short: A loop lets the network remember.

title: Backpropagation Through Time
subject: Neural Networks
statement: BPTT unrolls a recurrent network over time and backpropagates on the resulting graph.
detail: Long sequences make a deep graph.
proof: Apply the chain rule along time.

title: Vanishing Gradients in Long Sequences
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Repeated multiplication by the same Jacobian can make gradients decay exponentially with sequence length.
short: Old information is hard to learn.
detail: Exploding gradients are the companion issue.
proof: Multiply Jacobians along the unrolled path.

title: LSTM Gating
subject: Neural Networks
statement: LSTM uses input forget and output gates plus a cell state to control information flow.
detail: The cell has an additive gradient path.

title: Gated Recurrent Unit
subject: Neural Networks
statement: GRU simplifies LSTM with reset and update gates and no separate cell state.

title: Transformer Block
subject: Neural Networks
statement: The transformer replaces recurrence with stacked self attention and feedforward blocks.
proof: Stack attention and feedforward with residual links.

title: Scaled Dot Product Attention
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Attention computes weighted averages of values using softmax of scaled query key products.

title: Multi Head Attention
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Multi head attention runs several attention functions in parallel on different projections.
detail: It is an architectural design choice.

title: Positional Encoding
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Positional encodings inject order information into permutation invariant attention.
detail: Without them attention sees a bag of tokens.

title: Self Attention Has Quadratic Cost
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Full attention over n tokens computes an n by n score matrix.
detail: Sparse and linear variants try to help.

title: Residual Connections
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Residual blocks add the input to a transformed version of itself.

title: Residuals Ease Optimization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Identity skip paths give gradients a direct route through deep networks.

title: Batch Normalization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Batch normalization standardizes activations using batch statistics and learned scale and shift.
proof: Compute batch moments and affine transform.

title: Layer Normalization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Layer normalization standardizes across features per example independently of the batch.

title: Dropout
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Dropout randomly zeroes activations during training and scales the rest.
detail: Full network is used at test time.

title: Dropout as Approximate Averaging
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Dropout approximately averages many thinned networks with exact equivalence only for linear models.
short: It behaves like an ensemble heuristic.
detail: Expectations match only in simple cases.

title: Weight Decay
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Weight decay shrinks parameters each step and equals L2 regularization for plain SGD.
detail: With adaptive optimizers equivalence can break.

title: Autoencoder
subject: Neural Networks
statement: An autoencoder learns an identity map through a bottleneck representation.

title: Variational Autoencoder
subject: Neural Networks
statement: A VAE learns probabilistic encoder and decoder by maximizing the ELBO with a latent prior.
latex: \mathcal L=\mathbb{E}_{q(z\mid x)}[\log p(x\mid z)]-D_{KL}(q(z\mid x)\parallel p(z))
detail: The KL term regularizes the latent space.
proof: Apply variational inference with amortized encoder.

title: Reparameterization Trick
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Gaussian latent samples can be written as a deterministic function of fixed noise, permitting backpropagation.

title: GAN Minimax Objective
subject: Neural Networks
statement: A GAN trains a generator and discriminator in a two player game.
short: A forger and detector improve together.
detail: At equilibrium distributions match in ideal settings.

title: GAN Training Instability
subject: Neural Networks
statement: GAN optimization can oscillate or collapse because it is a game not a single objective.

title: Diffusion Forward Process
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Forward diffusion gradually adds Gaussian noise until data is nearly pure noise.
proof: Combine Gaussian steps by variance additivity.

title: Diffusion Models Learn to Denoise
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Reversing the noising process with a learned denoiser yields samples from the data distribution.
proof: Fit reverse conditionals using forward posteriors.

title: Denoising Estimates the Score
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Predicting noise at a corrupted point is equivalent to estimating the gradient of the log density of the smoothed data.

title: Message Passing in GNNs
subject: Neural Networks
statement: GNNs update node representations by aggregating information from neighbours.

title: Over Smoothing in Deep GNNs
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Many message passing layers can make node representations converge and become indistinguishable.

title: Attention Is Permutation Equivariant
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Self attention without positional encodings treats tokens as a set.

title: Xavier Initialization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Initial weights scaled by fan in and fan out help keep activation variances stable.

title: He Initialization
subject: Neural Networks
statement: For ReLU nets variance two over fan in accounts for half the activations being zeroed.

title: Transfer Learning
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Features learned on a large source task can be reused for a related target task.
detail: Works when tasks share structure empirically.

title: Fine Tuning
subject: Neural Networks
statement: Fine tuning continues training a pretrained model on task data with a lower learning rate.
proof: Run gradient steps on target data.

title: Neural Tangent Kernel
subject: Neural Networks
statement: In the infinite width limit network training follows kernel gradient descent with the neural tangent kernel.
short: Wide nets behave like kernel machines.
proof: Take the width limit of gradient flow.

title: Gradient Descent
subject: Optimization
statement: Gradient descent iteratively moves in the negative gradient direction.
detail: Step size controls speed and stability.
proof: Apply the first order descent direction.

title: Negative Gradient Is Steepest Descent
subject: Optimization
statement: The negative gradient is the steepest descent direction in Euclidean norm.
proof: Minimize the linear approximation over the unit ball.

title: Smooth Convex Convergence of Gradient Descent
subject: Optimization
statement: For convex L smooth functions with step one over L gradient descent reduces the gap at rate one over t.
detail: Use the descent lemma and convexity.

title: Strong Convexity Gives Linear Convergence
subject: Optimization
statement: For strongly convex smooth functions gradient descent with step one over L converges linearly.
consequence: Faster rates for well conditioned problems.

title: Convex Function Definition
subject: Optimization
statement: A function is convex when it lies below the chord between any two points.
detail: Differentiable convexity equals the gradient inequality.

title: Strong Convexity Definition
subject: Optimization
statement: Strong convexity adds a positive quadratic lower bound to convexity.
proof: Add a quadratic to a convex function.

title: L Smoothness Definition
subject: Optimization
statement: L smoothness means the gradient is L Lipschitz.

title: Stochastic Gradient Descent
subject: Optimization
statement: SGD updates using an unbiased gradient estimate from one or a few samples.
detail: Noise falls with mini batch size.
proof: Sample an index and compute its gradient.

title: Stochastic Gradient Is Unbiased
subject: Optimization
statement: Uniform index sampling makes the stochastic gradient equal the full gradient in expectation.

title: Robbins Monro Step Size Conditions
subject: Optimization
statement: For convex stochastic objectives step sizes with divergent sum and square summable values give convergence.
short: Shrink steps but not too fast.

title: Momentum
subject: Optimization
statement: Momentum accumulates an exponentially decaying average of past gradients.

title: Nesterov Accelerated Gradient
subject: Optimization
statement: Nesterov momentum evaluates the gradient at a look ahead point.

title: Accelerated Rate Is Optimal
subject: Optimization
statement: No first order method beats one over t squared for smooth convex functions in the black box model.
short: The accelerated rate cannot improve generally.

title: Adam Optimizer
subject: Optimization
statement: Adam maintains decaying averages of gradients and squared gradients and normalizes each coordinate.

title: Adam Bias Correction
subject: Optimization
statement: Dividing moving averages by one minus beta to the t removes initialization bias.

title: Adaptive Optimizers Can Fail
subject: Optimization
statement: Uncorrected adaptive methods can fail on some convex problems where SGD succeeds.
latex: RMSProp style scaling can diverge on constructed examples
short: Adaptive scaling is not universally safe.
proof: Exhibit gradients with decaying small components.

title: Newton Method
subject: Optimization
statement: Newton method uses curvature to take a Hessian aware step.
short: Use the Hessian to choose the step.

title: Newton Local Quadratic Convergence
subject: Optimization
statement: Near a minimizer with positive definite Hessian Newton error squares each iteration.
proof: Bound the remainder by Lipschitz continuity.

title: Quasi Newton Methods
subject: Optimization
statement: Quasi Newton methods replace the Hessian by an approximation updated from gradient differences.

title: The Secant Condition
subject: Optimization
statement: Quasi Newton updates enforce that the Hessian approximation maps the step to the gradient change.
detail: Finite difference analogue of Hessian times step.

title: BFGS Update
subject: Optimization
statement: BFGS updates a positive definite Hessian approximation with a rank two formula satisfying the secant condition.
latex: B_{t+1}=B_t-\frac{B_t s_t s_t^\top B_t}{s_t^\top B_t s_t}+\frac{y_t y_t^\top}{y_t^\top s_t}
detail: Preserves positivity when y transpose s is positive.

title: L BFGS
subject: Optimization
statement: L BFGS stores only a few correction pairs and applies quasi Newton steps implicitly.
detail: Memory is linear in stored pairs.

title: KKT Conditions
subject: Optimization
statement: Under constraint qualifications KKT conditions are necessary for smooth constrained optimality and sufficient for convex problems.

title: Complementary Slackness
subject: Optimization
statement: At a KKT point each inequality multiplier is zero unless its constraint is active.
detail: Follows from dual feasibility and stationarity.

title: Slater Condition
subject: Optimization
statement: Slater condition requires a strictly feasible point for convex inequalities.

title: Weak Duality
subject: Optimization
statement: The dual objective always lower bounds the primal minimum.
short: Dual bound never exceeds primal optimum.
detail: Evaluate the Lagrangian at the primal optimum.

title: Strong Duality under Convexity
subject: Optimization
statement: Convex problems satisfying Slater condition have no duality gap.

title: Lagrangian Function
subject: Optimization
statement: The Lagrangian folds constraints into the objective with multipliers.

title: Line Search
subject: Optimization
statement: Line search chooses a step length along a direction by approximate one dimensional minimization.

title: Backtracking Line Search
subject: Optimization
statement: Backtracking shrinks a trial step until a sufficient decrease condition holds.

title: Armijo Condition
subject: Optimization
statement: Armijo condition requires decrease proportional to step length and directional derivative.

title: Wolfe Conditions
subject: Optimization
statement: Wolfe conditions combine sufficient decrease with a curvature condition on the directional derivative.
latex: \nabla f(x+\alpha d)^\top d\ge c_2\nabla f(x)^\top d

title: Coordinate Descent
subject: Optimization
statement: Coordinate descent optimizes one variable at a time cycling through coordinates.
short: Optimize one coordinate at a time.

title: Proximal Gradient Method
subject: Optimization
statement: Proximal gradient handles smooth plus nonsmooth objectives by a gradient step followed by a proximal map.
detail: Converges at one over t for convex f.

title: Prox of L1 Is Soft Thresholding
subject: Optimization
statement: The proximal operator of lambda times L1 norm is componentwise soft thresholding.
detail: Solve a one dimensional quadratic plus absolute value.

title: Positive Definite Hessian Implies Local Minimum
subject: Optimization
statement: Zero gradient plus positive definite Hessian implies a strict local minimum.

title: Random Reshuffling
subject: Optimization
statement: Shuffling data before each epoch usually improves SGD performance over fixed ordering.

title: Markov Decision Process
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: An MDP models sequential decisions with states actions transitions rewards and a discount.
short: Formal model of an agent environment loop.
detail: Next state and reward depend only on state and action.

title: Markov Property
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: The future is conditionally independent of the past given the present state.

title: Discounted Return
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: The discounted return sums future rewards with geometric weights.

title: Bellman Expectation Equation
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: The value of a state equals expected immediate reward plus discounted expected next value.
short: Value decomposes into now plus later.
proof: Condition on first action and next state.

title: Bellman Optimality Equation
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: The optimal value satisfies a max over actions of reward plus discounted next value.
short: Optimal value is a fixed point.

title: Value Iteration
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Value iteration repeatedly applies the Bellman optimality operator to a value estimate.

title: Bellman Operator Is a Contraction
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: For discount below one the Bellman optimality operator is a contraction in sup norm.
short: Value iteration converges by Banach theorem.

title: Policy Iteration
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Policy iteration alternates policy evaluation and greedy improvement.

title: Policy Improvement Theorem
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: A policy greedy with respect to another policy value has value at least as large everywhere.

title: Q Learning
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Q learning updates action values toward reward plus discounted maximum next value off policy.
detail: Target uses max not action taken.

title: Q Learning Convergence
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Tabular Q learning converges to optimal action values with sufficient visits and decaying steps.
detail: It is stochastic approximation with optimality operator.

title: SARSA
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: SARSA updates values using the reward and the next action actually chosen by the policy.

title: Q Learning Versus SARSA
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Q learning is off policy and optimistic while SARSA is on policy and accounts for exploration.

title: Temporal Difference Learning
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: TD methods update estimates using other learned estimates, bootstrapping from successors.
short: Learn from a guess about the future.
detail: Bootstrapping distinguishes TD from Monte Carlo.
proof: Combine reward and estimated future value.

title: TD Error
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: The TD error is the difference between the observed target and current prediction.

title: Monte Carlo RL
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Monte Carlo methods estimate value by averaging complete returns.

title: Monte Carlo Versus TD Variance
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Monte Carlo has high variance and no bootstrapping bias while TD has lower variance and some bias.
latex: \text{MC: unbiased high variance; TD: biased low variance}

title: Policy Gradient Theorem
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Expected return gradient equals expectation of score times action value.

title: REINFORCE
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: REINFORCE samples trajectories and weights log action probabilities by returns.
proof: Sample episodes and apply the theorem.

title: Baseline Reduces Policy Gradient Variance
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Subtracting a state dependent baseline leaves the expected gradient unchanged but reduces variance.
short: Baselines do not bias the gradient.
detail: Score times state only function has zero mean.

title: Actor Critic
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Actor critic methods maintain a policy and a learned value function used to reduce variance.
proof: Combine policy gradient and value learning.

title: Advantage Function
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Advantage measures how much better an action is than average in a state.

title: Epsilon Greedy Exploration
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Epsilon greedy chooses a random action with probability epsilon and greedy otherwise.

title: Multi Armed Bandit
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: A bandit is a one state decision problem with unknown reward distributions per action.

title: Bandit Regret
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Regret is expected loss from not always choosing the best arm.

title: UCB1 Algorithm
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: UCB1 selects the arm maximizing empirical mean plus a shrinking exploration bonus.

title: UCB1 Has Logarithmic Regret
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: UCB1 regret grows at most logarithmically in horizon up to a constant depending on gaps.
detail: Bound times a suboptimal arm is chosen.

title: Thompson Sampling
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Thompson sampling chooses actions according to posterior probability of optimality.

title: Exploration versus Exploitation
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: An agent trades gathering information against maximizing immediate reward.
short: Try new things or use the best known?

title: Experience Replay
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Storing and reusing transitions breaks correlations and improves data efficiency in deep RL.

title: Deep Q Network
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: DQN approximates Q values with a network stabilized by replay and a target network.

title: Model Based versus Model Free RL
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Model based methods use a transition model while model free methods learn values or policies directly.
short: Learn the world or learn to act?

title: Importance Sampling for Off Policy Evaluation
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Off policy evaluation reweights behaviour trajectories by likelihood ratios.

title: Eligibility Traces
subject: Reinforcement Learning
statement: Eligibility traces combine TD and Monte Carlo ideas with decaying visit traces.

title: Bayesian Network Factorization
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A Bayesian network is a directed acyclic graph whose joint distribution factorizes into local conditionals given parents.
proof: Apply chain rule and read parents.

title: D Separation
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: D separation is a graph criterion for conditional independence implied by a Bayesian network.
latex: X\perp\!\!\!\perp Y\mid Z\ \text{if all paths blocked}
detail: Colliders differ from chains and forks.

title: Markov Blanket
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A Markov blanket is the set of parents children and children spouses of a node.
detail: Minimal conditioning set for local prediction.
proof: Identify nodes making X independent of rest.

title: Conditional Independence
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Variables are conditionally independent given Z when the joint conditional factors.
latex: \mathbb P(X,Y\mid Z)=\mathbb P(X\mid Z)\mathbb P(Y\mid Z)
detail: Written X perpendicular Y given Z.

title: Hidden Markov Model
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: An HMM is a Markov chain of latent states with conditionally independent observations.
latex: \mathbb P(x_{1:T},z_{1:T})=\mathbb P(z_1)\prod_t\mathbb P(z_t\mid z_{t-1})\mathbb P(x_t\mid z_t)

title: Forward Backward Algorithm
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Forward backward computes hidden state marginals in an HMM by dynamic programming.
detail: Cost is quadratic in states times length.

title: Viterbi Algorithm
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Viterbi finds the most likely hidden state sequence using max instead of sum.

title: Expectation Maximization
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: EM alternates posterior latent responsibilities and maximizing expected complete data log likelihood.
detail: Handles latent variables via a bound.

title: EM Monotonicity
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Every EM iteration does not decrease observed data log likelihood.
detail: E step closes the Jensen gap.
proof: Decompose likelihood into ELBO plus KL.

title: Gaussian Mixture Model
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A GMM models a density as a weighted sum of Gaussian components.
detail: Weights are nonnegative and sum to one.

title: EM for Gaussian Mixtures
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: EM for mixtures computes soft responsibilities then refits components to weighted data.

title: Variational Inference
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Variational inference approximates an intractable posterior by optimizing over a tractable family.

title: Evidence Lower Bound
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Log marginal likelihood equals ELBO plus KL divergence from approximation to posterior.
proof: Write log of p(x,z) over q expectation.

title: Mean Field Approximation
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Mean field VI restricts the variational family to fully factorized distributions.

title: Coordinate Ascent Variational Inference
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: CAVI optimizes each mean field factor in turn holding others fixed.
short: Update one factor at a time.

title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: MCMC builds a Markov chain with target stationary distribution and uses samples for integration.
short: Sample a hard distribution by walking.

title: Metropolis Hastings Algorithm
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Metropolis Hastings proposes moves and accepts with a ratio correcting proposal asymmetry.

title: Detailed Balance
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A chain satisfies detailed balance when pairwise probability flows balance.
proof: Sum over y to get pi T equals pi.

title: Gibbs Sampling
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Gibbs sampling updates each variable from its full conditional given the others.

title: Importance Sampling Estimator
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Importance sampling estimates expectations under p using weighted samples from proposal q.
detail: High variance if proposal misses target.

title: Particle Filter
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A particle filter approximates filtering distributions by propagating and resampling weighted samples.
short: Sequential Monte Carlo for state estimation.

title: Beta Binomial Conjugacy
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A beta prior on a Bernoulli parameter yields a beta posterior after binomial data.

title: Dirichlet Multinomial Conjugacy
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A Dirichlet prior is conjugate to a multinomial likelihood.

title: Collider Explaining Away
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Conditioning on a common effect can induce dependence between independent causes.
detail: Colliders must not be conditioned on naively.

title: Belief Propagation
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Belief propagation passes messages between nodes to compute marginals on factor graphs.

title: Junction Tree Algorithm
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Junction tree performs exact inference by clustering variables into a clique tree.

title: Loopy Belief Propagation
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Running belief propagation on cyclic graphs often works well without general exactness.
latex: \text{loopy fixed points need not be exact marginals}

title: MCMC Mixing Time
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: MCMC bias decreases as the chain approaches stationarity at a rate governed by mixing time.

title: Conditional Random Field
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A CRF models labels given observations with an undirected graphical model.

title: Latent Variable Model
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: A latent variable model uses unobserved variables to explain dependence among observations.

title: MCMC versus Variational Inference
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: MCMC is asymptotically exact but slow while variational inference is fast but biased by family choice.
short: Sampling exact in limit VI approximate.

title: Jensen Inequality for Log Likelihood
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Concavity of log yields a lower bound on log marginal likelihood.

title: Amortized Inference
subject: Probabilistic AI
statement: Amortized inference uses a learned function to output variational parameters per example.

title: Tokenization
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Tokenization splits text into units such as words subwords or characters.
detail: Choice affects vocabulary and rare words.

title: Byte Pair Encoding
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: BPE builds a subword vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent adjacent symbol pair.
proof: Count adjacent pairs and merge greedily.

title: WordPiece
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: WordPiece merges pairs chosen by likelihood gain rather than raw frequency.

title: Subword Vocabulary Trade Off
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Smaller vocabularies handle rare words better but yield longer sequences.
detail: Engineering trade off not a theorem.

title: Distributional Hypothesis
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Words in similar contexts tend to have similar meanings.
short: Know a word by its company.

title: Dense Embeddings versus One Hot
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Dense embeddings encode similarity while one hot vectors treat all words as equally distant.

title: Word2Vec Skip Gram
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Skip gram learns embeddings by predicting surrounding words from a centre word.
proof: Train shallow net on moving windows.

title: Continuous Bag of Words
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: CBOW predicts the centre word from its surrounding context.

title: GloVe
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: GloVe learns embeddings by factorizing global co occurrence statistics with weighted least squares.

title: Contextual Embeddings
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Contextual models assign different vectors to the same word in different sentences.
short: A word meaning depends on context.

title: Autoregressive Language Modeling
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Autoregressive LM factorizes sequence probability into next token conditionals.

title: Perplexity
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Perplexity is the exponential of average negative log likelihood per token.

title: Perplexity Equals Exponent of Cross Entropy
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Perplexity is two to cross entropy in bits or e to it in nats.

title: N Gram Language Model
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: An n gram model approximates next word probability from the previous n minus one words.

title: Markov Assumption in N Grams
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: N gram models assume only a finite suffix matters.

title: Smoothing for N Grams
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Smoothing assigns probability to unseen n grams by shifting mass from seen ones.
detail: Add k and interpolation are heuristics.

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Seq2seq maps an input sequence to an output sequence with encoder and decoder.

title: Encoder Decoder Attention
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Attention lets the decoder query all encoder states instead of one compressed vector.
short: Look back at source while generating.

title: Masked Language Modeling
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Masked LM trains a bidirectional model to recover randomly masked tokens.

title: Autoregressive Pretraining
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: GPT style models are pretrained to predict next token then adapted to tasks.

title: Scaling Laws as Empirical Observations
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Loss often follows smooth power laws in model size data and compute over wide ranges.
detail: Empirical regularity not a theorem; extrapolation can fail.

title: Compute Optimal Scaling
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: For fixed compute, more tokens with smaller models can beat larger models on fewer tokens.

title: In Context Learning
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Large language models can perform tasks from prompt examples without weight updates.

title: Chain of Thought Prompting
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Prompting for intermediate reasoning steps can improve multi step task performance.

title: BLEU Score
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: BLEU measures translation quality by modified n gram precision with brevity penalty.

title: ROUGE Score
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: ROUGE measures summarization quality via overlap with references.

title: Exact Match and Human Evaluation
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Exact match is cheap but strict while human evaluation is faithful but costly.
short: Automatic metrics trade fidelity for speed.

title: Part of Speech Tagging
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: POS tagging assigns grammatical categories to tokens in context.

title: Named Entity Recognition
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: NER identifies and classifies mentions of people organizations and places.

title: Machine Translation Objective
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Machine translation maps text between languages by modelling target conditional probability.

title: Multilingual Tokenization Fragmentation
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Tokenizers fitted to English heavy corpora can fragment other languages into many tokens.

title: Byte Level Language Models
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Byte level tokenization represents text as bytes so any string is encodable.

title: Digital Image as Tensor
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A digital image is a grid of pixel values arranged in channels such as red green and blue.
detail: Channels may encode colour or depth.

title: Convolution Operation
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Convolution slides a kernel over an image computing a weighted local sum at each position.
short: Local weighted sums with a filter.
proof: Slide kernel and compute dot products.

title: Cross Correlation versus Convolution
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Deep learning libraries use cross correlation which equals convolution with a flipped kernel.
short: Flipping is absorbed in learned weights.

title: Padding in Convolution
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Padding adds border values so convolution can preserve spatial size.

title: Stride in Convolution
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Stride is the step between successive kernel positions.

title: Receptive Field
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A unit receptive field is the input image region that can affect its activation.
detail: Grows with kernel size and stride.

title: Translation Equivariance of CNNs
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A CNN feature map shifts when the input shifts up to boundary and pooling effects.
detail: Pooling trades exact equivariance for tolerance.

title: Pooling for Local Invariance
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Pooling reduces sensitivity to small shifts by discarding precise position.
detail: Heuristic not a theorem of invariance.

title: Edge Detection Kernels
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Finite difference kernels respond to intensity changes and act as simple edge detectors.

title: Hierarchical Feature Learning
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Early CNN layers learn simple features while deeper layers combine them into complex shapes.

title: ImageNet Benchmark
subject: Computer Vision
statement: ImageNet is a large labelled image dataset whose competition catalyzed deep learning.
short: A benchmark that changed the field.

title: Object Detection Task
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Object detection locates instances with bounding boxes and assigns class labels.

title: Intersection over Union
subject: Computer Vision
statement: IoU measures box overlap as intersection area divided by union area.

title: Non Maximum Suppression
subject: Computer Vision
statement: NMS removes redundant detections by keeping highest scoring boxes and suppressing overlapping ones.

title: Region Based Detection
subject: Computer Vision
statement: R CNN style detectors first propose candidate regions then classify them.

title: Single Shot Detection
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Single shot detectors predict boxes and classes directly from feature maps in one pass.

title: Semantic Segmentation
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Semantic segmentation assigns a class label to every pixel.
detail: Does not separate same class instances.

title: Instance Segmentation
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Instance segmentation detects objects and labels pixels of each separate instance.

title: Fully Convolutional Networks
subject: Computer Vision
statement: FCNs replace classifier dense layers with convolutions for dense outputs.

title: U Net Architecture
subject: Computer Vision
statement: U Net uses symmetric encoder decoder with skip connections for precise localization.

title: Data Augmentation
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Augmenting images with label preserving transforms can improve generalization empirically.

title: Vision Transformer
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A vision transformer splits images into patches and applies a transformer to patch embeddings.

title: Colour Space Conversion
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Colour spaces differ in separating luminance from chrominance which matters for tasks.

title: Image Classification Task
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Image classification assigns one class label to an entire image.

title: Mixup Augmentation
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Mixup trains on convex combinations of images and labels encouraging smoother boundaries.

title: Translation Invariance in Recognition
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A classifier should label an object the same after it moves in the image.

title: Convolutional Neural Network
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A convolutional neural network stacks convolutional nonlinear and pooling layers.

title: Feature Map
subject: Computer Vision
statement: A feature map is the output grid produced by applying a filter across an image.

title: Anchor Boxes
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Anchor boxes are predefined shapes used by detectors to predict offsets.
detail: Matched to ground truth by IoU.

title: Semantic versus Instance Segmentation Distinction
subject: Computer Vision
statement: Semantic segmentation labels classes while instance segmentation separates individual objects.

title: Adversarial Examples
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Small imperceptible perturbations can cause trained models to make confident wrong predictions.

title: Fast Gradient Sign Method
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: FGSM creates an adversarial example by stepping in the sign of the loss gradient.

title: Adversarial Training
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Training on adversarial examples improves robust accuracy but can reduce standard accuracy.
detail: Accuracy robustness trade off is empirical.

title: Distribution Shift
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Distribution shift occurs when test data distribution differs from training distribution.

title: Covariate Shift
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Covariate shift changes p of x while p of y given x is fixed.

title: Label Shift
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Label shift changes class proportions while class conditionals stay fixed.

title: Overconfidence under Shift
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Neural nets often assign high probability to wrong answers on out of distribution inputs.

title: Expected Calibration Error
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: ECE bins predictions and measures gap between average confidence and accuracy.

title: Temperature Scaling
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Temperature scaling divides logits by a learned scalar to soften probabilities.

title: Saliency Maps
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Saliency maps highlight input features with largest gradient magnitude for a prediction.
detail: A heuristic explanation, not proof of cause.

title: LIME
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: LIME explains a single prediction by fitting a simple interpretable model locally.
proof: Perturb around x and fit linear model.

title: SHAP Values
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: SHAP assigns feature contributions satisfying efficiency symmetry dummy and additivity axioms.

title: Feature Visualization
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Optimizing an input to maximize a neuron activation can reveal what it detects.
detail: Shows preferred features not necessarily causal role.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Mechanistic interpretability aims to reverse engineer circuits and algorithms inside models.
detail: A research program not a single theorem.

title: Sparse Autoencoder Features
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Sparse autoencoders are used as an empirical method to find interpretable latent features.

title: Alignment as an Open Problem
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Aligning model behaviour with human intentions remains an open problem.
short: Open. No general solution is known.
detail: Specification is hard and values plural.

title: Reward Hacking
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Agents can exploit loopholes in a reward function rather than accomplish the intended task.
short: Optimize the proxy not the goal.

title: Scalable Oversight
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Scalable oversight studies how humans can supervise systems that outperform them on tasks.

title: Calibration Does Not Imply Accuracy
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: A perfectly calibrated predictor can be uninformative, such as always predicting the base rate.

title: Membership Inference
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Membership inference attacks infer whether an example was in training from model outputs.

title: Differential Privacy Definition
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Differential privacy bounds how much a computation output changes when one record changes.
detail: Neighbouring datasets differ in one record.

title: Fairness through Unawareness Fails
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Ignoring a protected attribute need not yield fair outcomes because other features correlate with it.

title: Robustness Accuracy Trade Off
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Empirically, increasing adversarial robustness often lowers clean accuracy.

title: Explanation Fidelity
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: An explanation can be fluent yet unfaithful to the model actual computation.

title: Out of Distribution Detection
subject: AI Safety & Interpretability
statement: Detecting whether an input comes from the training distribution remains difficult.

title: Finite Class PAC Sample Bound
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: For a finite hypothesis class a consistent learner needs O of epsilon squared inverse times log class size plus log one over delta examples.

title: VC Dimension Definition
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: VC dimension is the largest number of points a class can shatter.

title: Sauer Shelah Lemma
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: A class of VC dimension d labels n points in at most sum of binomial coefficients up to d ways.

title: Growth Function
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: The growth function counts the maximum number of labelings induced on n points.
detail: It upper bounds effective class size.

title: Fundamental Theorem of Statistical Learning
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: A class is PAC learnable exactly when its VC dimension is finite.
detail: Sufficiency uses uniform convergence; necessity uses shattering.
proof: Combine Sauer Shelah with lower bounds.

title: ERM Generalization Bound via VC
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: For a class of VC dimension d, with high probability excess risk is bounded by O of square root of d log n over n.

title: VC Dimension of Intervals
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: The class of intervals on the real line has VC dimension two.
short: Two points can be shattered three cannot.
detail: Any three ordered points cannot realize plus minus plus.

title: VC Dimension of Halfspaces
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Linear threshold classifiers in R^d have VC dimension d plus one.
short: Radon theorem gives the upper bound.
proof: Use Radon partition for three plus d points.

title: VC Dimension of Axis Aligned Rectangles
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Axis aligned rectangles in R^d have VC dimension two d.
detail: Two points per coordinate can be shattered.

title: PAC Lower Bound from VC
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Any learner for a class of VC dimension d needs at least on the order of d over epsilon examples.
short: No learner beats the VC scaling.
detail: Construct a hard distribution on shattered points.
proof: Use Fano or Assouad style argument.
consequence: Matches upper bounds up to logs.

title: Rademacher Complexity
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Rademacher complexity measures how well a class correlates with random signs.

title: Rademacher Generalization Bound
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: With high probability risk is at most empirical risk plus twice Rademacher complexity plus a confidence term.

title: Hoeffding Inequality
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Bounded independent averages concentrate around expectation with subgaussian tails.

title: McDiarmid Inequality
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Functions with bounded differences concentrate around expectation.

title: Dudley Entropy Integral
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Rademacher complexity is bounded by an integral of metric entropy of the class.

title: Covering Number Definition
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: A covering number is the fewest balls of radius epsilon needed to cover a set.
short: How many small balls cover the class.

title: Fat Shattering Dimension
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Fat shattering dimension generalizes VC dimension to real valued functions using margins.
detail: Reduces to VC for binary functions.

title: Bayes Classifier Optimality
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: The classifier choosing the most probable label minimizes expected zero one risk.

title: Bayes Error Rate
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Bayes error is the unavoidable risk of the optimal classifier.
detail: Cannot be beaten by any learner.

title: No Free Lunch Theorem
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Averaged uniformly over all data distributions every learning algorithm has the same expected out of sample error.
detail: Any advantage on some tasks is paid elsewhere.
wiki: No free lunch in search and optimization

title: Algorithmic Stability and Generalization
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Stable algorithms whose output changes little when one training point changes have small generalization gap.
proof: Replace one sample and bound loss change.

title: Leave One Out Estimate Bias
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Leave one out error is nearly unbiased for training size n minus one but can have high variance.
short: It estimates performance with one fewer example.

title: Sample Compression Scheme
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: A sample compression scheme stores a small subset of data sufficient to reconstruct a predictor.
detail: Many learning rules admit such schemes.

title: Minimum Description Length
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: MDL prefers models with short descriptions of both model and data.

title: Curse of Dimensionality
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Volume grows so fast in high dimensions that data become sparse and distance concentrates.

title: Manifold Hypothesis
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: High dimensional natural data are conjectured to lie near low dimensional manifolds.

title: Benign Overfitting
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Some interpolating models fit noisy training data yet generalize well.
proof: Analyze high dimensional min norm solutions.

title: Double Descent
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Test error can decrease increase then decrease again as model capacity grows beyond interpolation.
detail: Not predicted by classical bias variance.

title: Convex Surrogate Consistency
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: For classification, convex loss functions such as hinge and logistic are Fisher consistent under standard conditions.

title: Calibration of Surrogate Losses
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: A loss is calibrated if small surrogate risk implies small classification risk.

title: Uniform Convergence Definition
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Uniform convergence means empirical risks approach true risks simultaneously over a class.

title: Probably Approximately Correct Learning
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: PAC learning requires algorithms to output low error with high probability after polynomially many samples.
